beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:wonder, setting the scene]^Twice a year, Earth flies through the wreckage of a ^*comet*: a trail of dust and rubble strung around the ^Sun.
[d:tension][act:reporting the claim, even]Some say it's the comet that ^ended the Ice Age world. [gap:0.4][act:low, a hint of suspense][tune:fall]And it ^isn't finished.

[d:calm][act:plain, informative]The parent is comet ^Encke: a ball of ice and rock five kilometres across, on a ^three-year loop around the Sun. [p:0.93][act:explaining, an everyday picture]As it warms near the Sun, it sheds dust and grit, like a lorry shedding gravel along a ^road. [act:explaining, clear]Earth drives through that trail twice a year: in October and November, and again in late June and ^July.

[d:build][go:2|0][act:building, a real event]In {2015|twenty fifteen}, Earth crossed a ^dense knot of it, a swarm kept bunched together by the pull of ^Jupiter. [sfx:shimmer][act:delighted, vivid]Cameras caught a hundred and forty-four ^fireballs. [act:leaning in, weightier]And two ^asteroids in the knot, ^hundreds of metres wide.

[d:build][act:grave, storytelling]In {1908|nineteen oh eight}, something ^exploded in the sky over Siberia, and flattened two ^thousand square kilometres of forest: [p:0.93][act:explaining, a sense of scale]a square more than forty-five kilometres on each ^side. [act:explaining, careful]It burst in the air, so it left ^no crater. [act:pointed, lower][tune:fall]And it arrived in ^Taurid season.

[d:tension][go:4|0][act:laying out the claim, fair]So the idea, from two astronomers in the {1980s|nineteen eighties}: a ^giant comet broke up, long ago, and its pieces keep ^coming. [act:low, brief][tune:fall]In ^bursts.

[d:build][act:brisk, the test][tune:fall]Then, in {2025|twenty twenty-five}, astronomers ^counted. [p:0.93][act:explaining, an everyday picture]Break a giant comet, and you'd expect hundreds of big chunks, like the shards of a dropped ^plate. [act:precise, reading the result]Bodies over a hundred metres in the swarm: about ^nine to ^fourteen. [d:aside][act:gentle, pointed][tune:fall]Not the ^hundreds a giant would leave. [p:0.93][act:explaining, plain]The parent looks nearer ten kilometres across than a ^hundred. [act:dry, a small smile][tune:fall]Giants are hard to ^misplace.

[d:reveal][act:the turn, sincere][tune:fall]But the ^swarm is ^real. [act:clear, looking ahead]And it comes close@adj again in November {2032|^twenty thirty-two}, and June {2036|^twenty thirty-six}. [sfx:hit][act:practical, calm urgency][tune:fall]Specialists want telescopes ^ready, to spot any big rocks in it as it ^passes.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]A resonant ^swarm, held in step by Jupiter? [act:firm, certain][tune:highfall]^*Established*. [act:the next question, even][tune:rise]A ^giant comet behind the Younger Dryas, the sudden cold snap at the end of the Ice Age? [act:the verdict, level-headed][tune:fall]Not ^shown.
[d:tension][p:0.93][gap:0.4][act:the last word, quiet anticipation][tune:fall]The next test has a ^*date*.
